---
title: "Authorship & Contributorship Policy"
---

**Status:** Authoritative · **Owner:** PI · **Review:** Annually (authorship audit)

## 1. Purpose
To assign credit for RIPLRT scholarly products fairly, transparently, and consistently, and to prevent disputes by deciding authorship early and documenting it.

## 2. Scope
All scholarly products: manuscripts, abstracts, posters, presentations, reproducible notebooks, dashboards, briefs, and public-facing materials.

## 3. Authorship standard (ICMJE)
A person qualifies as an author only by meeting **all four** ICMJE criteria:
1. Substantial contributions to conception/design or acquisition/analysis/interpretation of data;
2. Drafting or critically revising for important intellectual content;
3. Final approval of the version to be published;
4. Agreement to be accountable for all aspects of the work.

Contributors not meeting all four are **acknowledged**, with their permission. Funding, supervision alone, or data collection alone do not, by themselves, confer authorship.

## 4. Contributorship (CRediT)
Every product records contributions using the CRediT taxonomy. The Authorship/Contributorship Agreement template captures this at project start and is updated as roles change.

## 5. Author order
- **First author:** led the intellectual/practical work.
- **Senior (last) author:** provided direction and holds accountability (typically the PI).
- **Middle authors:** ordered by contribution, discussed openly.
- **Student-first pathway:** when a mentee led the work, they receive first authorship. Developing mentees into first/co-first authors is an explicit group goal.

## 6. Process
1. Authorship is **discussed and documented at project start** (pod charter + agreement).
2. The plan is **revisited** at major milestones and at the annual authorship audit.
3. **Changes** require discussion with affected contributors and PI sign-off.

## 7. AI tools
AI tools are **never** authors — they cannot accept accountability. Material AI assistance is disclosed per the Responsible AI Use Policy and venue requirements.

## 8. Disputes
Raised early and directly; mediated by the PI against the documented agreement. Because plans are written at the start, most disputes are prevented.

## 9. Acknowledgments & attributions
Funders, data providers, and repositories are acknowledged using the **exact required language** of each source. Conflicts of interest are disclosed per venue and institution.
